identificationModule.briefTitle: A Phase II Clinical Study to Evaluate HLX43 in Subjects With Advanced Pancreatic Cancer
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Phase II Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of HLX43 (Anti-PD-L1 ADC) in Subjects With Advanced Pancreatic Cancer

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The study is being conducted to to explore the reasonable dosage and evaluate the efficacy, safety and tolerability of HLX43 (Anti-PD-L1 ADC) in Patients with Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This study is an open-label phase II clinical study to explore the reasonable dosage and evaluate the efficacy, safety and tolerability of HLX43 (Anti-PD-L1 ADC) in Patients with Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). In this study, eligible subjects will be randomized at 1:1 ratio, and the patients will be administered with HLX43 at different doses via intravenous infusion.

armGroups.label: HLX43 DOSE 1 (2.5 mg/kg)
armGroups.description: Patients with good tolerability and well controlled disease will receive the treatment once every 3 weeks (Q3W), Until disease progression, initiation of a new anti-tumor therapy, death, emergence of intolerable toxicity, or withdrawal of informed consent (whichever occurs first)

armGroups.label: HLX43 DOSE 2 (3.0 mg/kg)
armGroups.description: Patients with good tolerability and well controlled disease will receive the treatment once every 3 weeks (Q3W), Until disease progression, initiation of a new anti-tumor therapy, death, emergence of intolerable toxicity, or withdrawal of informed consent (whichever occurs first)

interventions.name: HLX43 DOSE 1 (2.5 mg/kg)
interventions.description: HLX43 is an anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody conjugated with a novel high potency DNA topoisomerase I (topo I) inhibitor, with a drug-antibody-ratio (DAR) of 8.

interventions.name: HLX43 DOSE 2 (3.0 mg/kg)
interventions.description: HLX43 is an anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody conjugated with a novel high potency DNA topoisomerase I (topo I) inhibitor, with a drug-antibody-ratio (DAR) of 8.

primaryOutcomes.description: Objective response rate (ORR) is the proportion of subjects with the best overall response being CR or PR (assessed by investigator per RECIST v1.1)
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From date of randomization until the date of first documented progression or date of death from any cause, whichever came first, assessed up to 24 weeks

primaryOutcomes.description: Defined as the time (in months) from randomization to the first confirmed and documented progressive disease or death (whichever occurs first) as assessed by INV per RECIST v1.1.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From date of randomization until the date of first documented progression or date of death from any cause, whichever came first, assessed up to 12 months

secondaryOutcomes.description: Objective response rate (ORR) (assessed by the IRRC per RECIST v1.1)
Defined as the time (in months) from randomization to the first confirmed and documented progressive disease or death (whichever occurs first) as assessed by the IRRC per RECIST v1.1.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From date of randomization until the date of first documented progression or date of death from any cause, whichever came first, assessed up to 12 months
From randomization to death from any cause (up to approximately 18 months)

secondaryOutcomes.description: Duration of response (DOR) is defined as the time from first response (CR or PR) until PD (RECIST v1.1) or death due to any cause, whichever occurs first.
Disease control rate (DCR) is defined as the proportion of subjects with a best overall response of CR, PR, or SD. Tumor response will be assessed by the investigator or IRRC as per RECIST v1.1.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Incidence and severity of adverse events (AEs)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Adverse events (AEs), serious adverse events (SAEs), laboratory tests, vital signs, 12-lead ECG, and physical examination
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: time from the date of the first dose of study drug until 90 days after last dose, assessed up to 18 months
